title: specs-from-code component inventory
description: Stack-agnostic inventory of ONE component (a service, app, worker, library or module): what it exposes (entry points), what it calls (outbound), what it stores, and how sure we are of each fact. The schema is the contract; how the inventory is produced (knowledge graph, code reading, an optional stack-specific scanner) is free. Unknown values are null with an explicit entry in warnings[] — never invented.

kind.description: What the component is, as observed.

scopePaths.description: Repo-relative paths that bound the component ("." for the whole repo).

baselineCommit.description: The commit the inventory describes. null only if the component is not under git (then a warning is required).

stacks.description: Every language/runtime/framework detected in scope. A polyglot component lists several.

entryPoints.description: The inbound surface: every way the outside world (users, other services, schedulers, operators, importing code) can trigger behavior. An empty array is valid only with a warning explaining why (e.g. a pure library scoped out).

outbound.description: Everything the component calls or emits: downstream HTTP/gRPC, messages produced, third-party SDKs, email/SMS, file drops.

target.description: Host/service/topic/provider as configured (never a secret value).

retries.description: Retry policy as observed, e.g. '3x exponential', 'none'.

usedBy.description: entryPoint ids that reach this call.

configuration.description: Behavior-changing configuration: feature flags, toggles, tenant/env switches. Names only — never values of secrets.

affects.description: entryPoint ids whose behavior it changes.

secret.description: true when the key holds a credential, token or connection string. Its value is never recorded anywhere.

coverage.description: Line coverage 0..1 from an existing report; null if no report exists (with a warning).

usageSource.description: Where usage numbers came from (access logs, APM, queue metrics, analytics). null when none was provided — then every usage is null.

warnings.description: Every degradation, gap or assumption, stated verbatim for the reader. Never empty by omission: if there are none, contain the single string 'none'.

source.description: How the fact was established. graph-inferred and docs never back a signed spec on their own.

ref.description: path:line, config key, graph node id, or doc path.

trigger.description: Kind-specific address of the entry point. Fill the fields that apply; leave the rest out.

operation.description: graphql Query/Mutation/Subscription field, grpc Service/Method, websocket event.

broker.description: message: sqs, kafka, rabbitmq, nats, pubsub, eventbridge…

symbol.description: library-export/function: exported name or function name.

handler.description: path:line of the code that handles it.

auth.description: Auth requirement as observed (e.g. 'bearer JWT, scope payments:write', 'none', 'mTLS'). null if not determinable.

usage.description: Observed volume in usageSource.window; null when no usage source (never guessed). 0 marks a dead-surface candidate.

capability.description: CAP-id assigned in the capability-map phase; null before it, and null when excluded.

exclusion.description: Set in the capability-map phase when the entry point is deliberately not assigned to a capability (capability stays null). Lets coverage be checked from the inventory alone.
